source.title_on_document: Scaffolding Recursive Divergence and Convergence in Story Ideation

paper_design_summary: Sixteen creative writers recruited through Upwork each modified supplied summaries of Cinderella and Alice in Wonderland using Reverger and a restricted version of the same AI tool in a counterbalanced within-person study; random assignment to sequences is not stated (pp. 6-7, Sections 5-5.4 and Table 1). Reverger supports recursive exploration of story directions and synthesis of multiple selected directions, while the baseline restricts these features (p. 6, Section 5.1). Evaluation used self-reported creativity support and workload, interviews, and interaction logs, without a creativity or diversity score on the produced stories (pp. 8-10, Sections 5.5-6.2.2 and Table 2).

studies.label: Counterbalanced story-ideation user study (randomization not stated)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Tool and story order across sessions: each participant used Reverger and the restricted AI baseline on different stories. The tool/story combinations were counterbalanced using a Latin Square; the mechanism for allocating participants to sequences is not stated.
assignment.quote: We employed the Latin Square design [24] (see Table 1 for details) to counterbalance the order of tools and stories.
assignment.locator: p. 6, Section 5 (User Study); p. 7, Table 1 and Section 5.4 (Procedure)

arms.name: Reverger
arms.description: AI tool permitting recursive exploration of high-level story directions and synthesis of multiple selected directions; the same participants also used the baseline (p. 6, Sections 5-5.1; p. 7, Table 1; p. 9, Table 2).

arms.name: Restricted AI baseline
arms.description: Reverger with recursive exploration and simultaneous selection of multiple directions disabled; users could explore directions and generate variations from a single selected direction (p. 6, Section 5.1). These are the same participants as in Reverger (p. 7, Table 1; p. 9, Table 2).

participants.who: Creative writers recruited from Upwork who self-identified as experts or hobbyists; participants held a range of occupations. The same people completed both tool conditions.
participants.quote: We conducted a user study with 16 participants, ranging from novice to expert writers, to evaluate Reverger’s effectiveness and impact on the creative story ideation workflow.
participants.locator: p. 14, Section 8 (quoted sample statement); pp. 6-7, Section 5.3 and Table 1 (recruitment, backgrounds and conditions); p. 9, Table 2 (log data for P1-P16 in both conditions)

ai_tool.name_model: Reverger and its restricted baseline; Anthropic claude-3-sonnet-20240229
ai_tool.how_used: Structured AI generation of abstract story directions, sub-directions, and rewritten passages: users highlight text, explore directions, select desired directions, and generate story variations. Reverger supports recursive exploration and synthesis of multiple directions; the baseline restricts these operations (p. 5, Section 4.2; p. 6, Section 5.1).

task.description: Freely modify supplied one-paragraph summaries of Cinderella and Alice in Wonderland by exploring and selecting variations of highlighted story passages (p. 6, Section 5.2; p. 7, Section 5.4.2).
task.duration: 10 minutes per task, with extra time allowed when participants requested it (p. 7, Section 5.4.2).

contrasts.reported: Reverger versus restricted AI baseline: exploration, z = −4.56, p = .038 (Wilcoxon Signed-Rank test, as printed); the paper reports better perceived exploration with Reverger. This is a tool-support self-report, not a score on creative output.
contrasts.locator: p. 8, Section 6.1 (Summary of Survey Results) and Figure 4a

outcomes.name: Creativity Support Index: results worth effort (self-report)
outcomes.question: none

contrasts.reported: Reverger versus restricted AI baseline: results worth effort, z = −4.82, p = .003 (Wilcoxon Signed-Rank test, as printed); the paper reports more effort-worthy outcomes with Reverger. This is a tool-support self-report, not a score on creative output.
contrasts.locator: p. 8, Section 6.1 (Summary of Survey Results) and Figure 4a

company_involvement.description: Yuqian Sun, Melissa Roemmele, Max Kreminski, and John Joon Young Chung list Midjourney affiliations. The document does not state a separate funding or sponsorship role.
company_involvement.locator: PDF p. 1, author names and institutional affiliations

eligibility.reason: Randomization is not stated: the methods describe Latin Square counterbalancing of tool/story order without explaining allocation to sequences (p. 6, Section 5; p. 7, Table 1 and Section 5.4). Only 16 distinct people were analyzed, with the same people in both conditions, below the 50-person threshold (pp. 6-7, Section 5.3 and Table 1; p. 9, Table 2). The reported quantitative ratings are CSI/NASA-TLX self-reports, and the interaction logs count directions revealed and generation attempts; no creativity or diversity score on participant-produced output is reported (p. 8, Sections 5.5-6.1; p. 9, Table 2; p. 10, Section 6.2.2). The survey outcomes are retained only to document the main findings. This small user study has no qualifying output-scored outcome and does not enter the core or a context evidence class.

one_line_finding: Among 16 participants (p. 9, Table 2), Reverger received higher self-reported exploration (z = −4.56, p = .038) and results-worth-effort ratings (z = −4.82, p = .003) than its restricted AI baseline (p. 8, Section 6.1); output creativity was not scored.
